title: Build a 4-bit counter with synchronous reset
statement_md: Create a module named `counter4`. On every rising edge of `clk`, if `reset` is 1 the 4-bit `count` becomes 0; otherwise it increments by 1. Reset is synchronous and active-high. After 15 the counter wraps to 0.

tests.hint: reset must be applied inside the clocked always block, sampled at posedge clk.

tests.purpose: ignores reset until the next edge
tests.hint: The event control should list clk only. An asynchronous reset reacts before the next edge, which is wrong here.
Check count <= count + 1 on the non-reset path.
State must advance exactly once per clock edge, not per delta cycle.
A 4-bit register wraps from 15 to 0 for free on overflow. No explicit wrap logic is needed.
reset must take priority over incrementing when both conditions could apply at the same edge.

hints: Everything happens on the rising edge, so one always_ff block on posedge clk is enough.
Check reset first inside that block so it wins over counting.
A 4-bit register wraps from 15 to 0 on its own. No extra logic is needed.
